source.title: Do Large Language Models Mirror Cognitive Language Processing?
source.authors: Yuqi Ren; Ren-Ren Jin; Tong-Xuan Zhang; De-Yi Xiong

record.tranche_reason: The paper measures representational similarity between LLMs and fMRI signals, not held-out cross-entropy loss, loss extrapolation, or compute-optimal parameter/token allocation. Its results do not test the listed versions.
record.gate_note: The paper cites scaling-law work and measures how model scale and pretraining checkpoints relate to LLM-brain similarity. That is a different outcome from the loss and allocation claims. Prompt, alignment, sentiment, and benchmark results also concern LLM-brain similarity rather than the listed versions.
record.test_reason: The study measures RSA similarity between LLM embeddings and fMRI signals across checkpoints, sizes, alignment stages and prompts. It measures no held-out loss, fits no power law, and does no extrapolation or compute-allocation analysis. Scale is not related to benchmark scores; benchmark scores are correlated with brain similarity using public numbers. Kaplan and Hoffmann are cited only to motivate the pretraining-data analysis. The claimed link to loss is the authors' inference ('indirectly suggests'), not a measurement.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct, with one omission. The authors also conclude that LLM-brain similarity correlates highly with benchmark performance (MMLU, HellaSwag, Chatbot Arena, AlpacaEval), so it could serve as an evaluation method. LLaMA3-70B-instruct is an outlier on the alignment evaluations.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses representational similarity analysis between model embeddings and fMRI representations rather than measuring held-out language-model loss or fitting scaling laws.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported outcome is assessed with different RSA similarity measures and across final versus intermediate layers; the paper says the broad trends remain consistent. Prompt strategy also changes LLM-brain similarity.

fits_no_version.finding: Amber LLM-brain RSA similarity rises gradually across 10 pretraining checkpoints (Figure 2, figure only).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: LLM-brain representational similarity increases with pretraining-data size.

fits_no_version.finding: LLaMA2 Pearson RSA similarity is 0.2207 at 7B, 0.2340 at 13B and 0.2568 at 70B. The same direction holds at intermediate layers (Table 3).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: LLM-brain representational similarity increases with model size within a family.

fits_no_version.finding: Aligned models (SFT/RLHF/DPO) score higher than their base models. For example, LLaMA2-13B-chat (0.2694) exceeds LLaMA2-70B (0.2568).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Alignment training raises LLM-brain similarity more than model scaling does.

record.problems: The measurements concern LLM-brain representational similarity rather than held-out loss. The Amber checkpoint values are shown only in a figure, without stated numerical values. The paper does not test compute-optimal allocations.
record.rows_left_out: Other model-size, training-stage, prompt, sentiment, layer, and benchmark results concern LLM-brain similarity or its association with evaluation scores, not any listed version's loss or allocation outcome.

untested.parts: No held-out loss is measured against parameters, tokens or compute.
No fits on small runs and no extrapolation to larger runs.
No comparison of model shape at fixed parameter count.
No power-law fits in other modalities or training regimes. fMRI data are used only as a comparison target.
Downstream scores are not related to scale or loss. They are correlated only with brain similarity, using public benchmark numbers.
No scaling-law fits whose sensitivity to setup or fitting choices could be examined.

record.verdict_notes: Relation set to cites_only. The scaling-law papers are cited as motivation, and the paper infers loss correlates negatively with similarity without measuring loss. No version is tested, so no verdict labels are given. R11-R13 keep the state 'observed' for the brain-similarity trend but link to no version.

versions.untested_parts: Held-out loss versus parameters, tokens, or compute.
Prediction of larger-run loss from smaller-run fits.
Compute-budget allocation between parameters and tokens.
Architecture effects on loss at fixed parameter count.
Power-law loss in other modalities or training regimes.
Downstream performance as predicted by scale or pretraining loss.
Dependence of loss-law fits or compute-optimal allocations on setup and fitting choices.

rows.subject: Amber
rows.operation_detail: Compared LLM-brain similarity across pretraining checkpoints representing different pretraining-data sizes.
rows.note: The paper says similarity improves gradually as pretraining data size increases; the plotted checkpoint value is not stated numerically.
rows.check: Single checkpoint read from Figure 2. No numeric value and no baseline, so an 'observed' state for one checkpoint is not meaningful. The trend belongs in fits_no_version, which already holds it.
